title: multilingual-classics-markdown: Public-domain literary classics in 54 languages, curated as markdown with YAML frontmatter
description:
A curated corpus of 146 books in 54 languages across 67 locales, converted from upstream digitisation projects to clean markdown with consistent YAML frontmatter. It spans 14 language families and 20 script systems: Latin with rich diacritics, Cyrillic, polytonic Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Perso-Arabic, Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Tibetan, Egyptian hieroglyphs, Han, kana, Hangul, the Thai abugida and the Cherokee syllabary, together with three constructed auxiliary languages and the historical stages of English from Old English to original-spelling Early Modern.

Every work is public domain in the United States. Each file records its source, the exact URL fetched, the edition it was transcribed from where that's known, its publication year, and notes on what was excerpted, corrected or left alone. Books whose text falls below the corpus fidelity bar carry a machine-readable text_quality tier, and books admitted under the sacred-text exception carry a sacred_text field.

This is a convenience corpus rather than a collection of critical editions. Texts inherit the transcription errors of the volunteer projects they come from, and none has been systematically collated against manuscripts or print editions. AI models were used to find sources, convert the texts and repair errors, under the maintainer's direction and responsibility. Most texts haven't been checked in this corpus by someone who reads the language, and corrections from such readers are welcome. Known defects are tracked openly in QUALITY.md; the scope is described in the README, and the method in CORPUS.md.

The book content is released under CC0 1.0. The conversion tooling under scripts/ is MIT-licensed.
